name: The Goodhue household — a documented physician in a reconstructed household (south division)
head: inf_physician_south_01

arrival.note: NOT AN ARRIVAL, A BOUND. Nothing dates a hypothesised household, and a year would be a claim nobody made. `not_later_than` the scene date states the only thing the inference carries: the town's need is measured on 1 July 1835, so the household is posited as being here by then and at no stated time before it.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not claimed. The layer infers households, not families: the person entries here are the ones the trade argument requires and nothing counts wives or children, because counting them would multiply a hypothesis by an invention.

origin.note: Not claimed. Where a hypothesised resident came from is unknowable by construction, and the documented layer's origins (Vermont, Washington, Ann Arbor) are evidence about those men and not a distribution to sample from.

reason_for_coming.note: Not claimed for the person. The reason the HOUSEHOLD is in the dataset is the trade argument in research_note, which is a statement about the town and not about a motive.

lives_at.note: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d7_035 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

works_at.note: physicians_office is a structure record this parcel raises for the purpose, because no roof of the right family stood free in this district. The workplace is assigned from the reconstruction schedule's workshop and store families for this trade.

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the scene date IS the hypothesis: this household exists in the dataset because the town of 1 July 1835 demonstrably needed households of this trade. It is not a finding about anybody's whereabouts.

persons.name: Josiah C. Goodhue

occupation.note: THE PAPERS NAME HIM A PHYSICIAN. 1834-02-04 c001 (p. 3, col. 2): “[Ann]ual Mee[t]ing of the Chicago Temperance Society. [T]his Society held its annual meeting, accor[ding] to appointment, in the Presbyterian Chur[c]h, [T]hursday evening, January 30, for the elec[tion] of officers for the ensuing year, and to lis[ten] to an address prepared for the occasion. [T]he following officer…”. The corpus names him 1 time(s), 1834-02-04 to 1834-02-04. THE HOUSEHOLD'S OWN ARGUMENT IS UNCHANGED and is why this roof is in the dataset at all: EIGHT PHYSICIANS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE 1833 TOWN AND THIS DATASET HELD NOT ONE DOCTOR'S OFFICE. Four are written as households in the documented layer. One further physician household is inferred to occupy the office this parcel builds, because naming that office for a documented doctor would attach a real man to an invented building.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON IN A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD, AND THE TWO HALVES OF THAT ARE GRADED SEPARATELY. The person is real and the papers name him: 1834-02-04 c001 (p. 3, col. 2), and 1 mention(s) between 1834-02-04 and 1834-02-04. WHERE HE LIVED AND WORKED IS STILL RECONSTRUCTED — the dwelling, the workplace and the division on this record are the ones the inferred-household programme dealt to the invented resident this replaces, and NOTHING HERE CLAIMS THEY ARE HIS. No source this project holds gives him an address; if one did, the register would have placed him and tools/retire_invented_residents.py would have refused him for that reason (refusal 5). This is what T-0264 retires: the town raised this household because it demonstrably needed the trade and had nobody documented to put in it, and it now has somebody. The invented name and its `name_basis` are gone with the invention. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1); the liberty taken is the housing, not the man.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 physician households in this layer, in the south division. EIGHT PHYSICIANS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE 1833 TOWN AND THIS DATASET HELD NOT ONE DOCTOR'S OFFICE. Four are written as households in the documented layer. One further physician household is inferred to occupy the office this parcel builds, because naming that office for a documented doctor would attach a real man to an invented building. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
